Markology for TMA Accounting

Your SEO Playbook

Use this each time you publish a page or a post. We start with what each part of a page does, then go through them one at a time with examples from your site and the new designs.

1. The parts2. Keywords3. Title tags4. Meta descriptions5. H1 headings6. Page layout7. URLs and images8. Internal links9. Blogs10. Schema11. Speed12. Backlinks13. Maps14. AI search15. Tracking16. Plan and checklist
1

Know the Parts of a Page

People often mix these up, so we’ll start here. A person sees your page twice: first as a listing in Google, then on your website. Different parts do different jobs, and you edit them in different places.

First, they see your listing in Google

Ctmasmallbusinessaccounting.com
AOne Team of Indianapolis CPAs for Books, Taxes & Payroll
BTMA is one team of Indianapolis CPAs and accountants. We keep your books, do your taxes, and run your payroll for one set monthly fee. Let’s chat.
  • ATitle tag. The blue link. It isn’t shown on your page. Its job is to get the click.
  • BMeta description. The gray text. It isn’t shown on your page either. It gives them a reason to choose you.
  • CURL. The page’s address. Your homepage is your domain, and every other page should have its keyword here, like /indianapolis-payroll-services.
They click, and your page opens ↓

Then, they see your page

DEFGH
  • DH1. The main heading on the page. Its job is to tell people they’re in the right place. Use one per page.
  • EFirst paragraph. Who you help, where and with what.
  • FCall to action. The next step.
  • GImage and alt text. Alt text is a hidden description of the photo.
  • HInternal links. Links to your other pages. The headings further down the page are called H2s.

This is the homepage design (option B) we sent you.

And Google reads code they never see

What it isSchema markup
Code that tells Google what the page is about.
Where people see itNowhere on the page. It can help how you show up.
Where you change it in HubSpotSettings, then Advanced
The ruleSee section 10
The mix-up to avoid: the title tag and the H1 are two different fields. Changing the H1 doesn’t change the blue link in Google. The title tag is written to win the click, and the H1 is written for someone who has already clicked.
2

Pick One Main Keyword for Each Page

A keyword is what someone types into Google. Each page needs its own, because two pages chasing the same one compete with each other.

What it isThe phrase you want the page to show up for
Where people see itIn what they search
Where you change it in HubSpotIt isn’t a field. You use it in the parts below.
The rule1 main keyword and 1 backup per page

The keyword sheet has every page, with searches and difficulty.

How to choose one for a new page

1Write down what a client would type
2Check searches and difficulty in SEMrush
3Google it. Are the results firms like you, or articles and directories?
4Make sure no other page of yours already uses it

Do this

  1. If the results are firms, build a service page. If they’re articles, write a blog post.
  2. Skip searches from people you don’t want, such as individual tax returns.
  3. Add the keyword and page to the sheet so nobody reuses it.
3

Write Title Tags Like a Salesperson

Your title tag sits next to nine other firms. Most say what they do and stop there. Yours needs the keyword and a reason to pick you.

What it isThe blue link in Google and the name on the browser tab
Where people see itGoogle results. Not on your page.
Where you change it in HubSpotPage: Settings, then General, then Page title
Post: Settings, then SEO title
The rule60 characters or less, keyword near the front, then the reason to click
Keyword+Reason to click

The reason can be a benefit, a problem you solve, proof, or the price question answered.

What a searcher sees

Now
tmasmallbusinessaccounting.com
Small Business Accounting in Indiana | TMA Accounting
TMA Accounting helps small business owners simplify bookkeeping, payroll, and taxes with one reliable team, clear guidance, and predictable support.
Change it to
tmasmallbusinessaccounting.com
One Team of Indianapolis CPAs for Books, Taxes & Payroll
TMA is one team of Indianapolis CPAs and accountants. We keep your books, do your taxes, and run your payroll for one set monthly fee. Let’s chat.

The old one describes a category. The new one has the keyword and the thing owners want, which is one team.

Titles you can use

PageTitle tag nowNew title tagWhy they’d click
HomepageSmall Business Accounting in Indiana | TMA AccountingOne Team of Indianapolis CPAs for Books, Taxes & Payroll56 charactersSays who, where and the one-team benefit
Monthly AccountingNew pageIndianapolis Accounting Services for One Set Monthly Fee56 charactersAnswers the price worry before they click
BookkeepingNew pageIndianapolis Bookkeeping Services | Get Your Books Caught Up60 charactersNames the problem they want gone
PayrollSmall Business Payroll Services in Indiana | TMA AccountingIndianapolis Payroll Services Tied to Your Books & Taxes56 charactersSays what a payroll company can’t
TaxNew pageIndianapolis Tax Accountants Who Know Your Books All Year57 charactersSays why you’re better than a once-a-year preparer
DentalNew pageDental CPAs: One Team for Books, Taxes & Payroll48 charactersSpeaks to one type of owner

Do this

  1. Write 3 versions before you pick one.
  2. Only promise what’s true on the page.
  3. Add the year to posts about deductions, limits, rates and deadlines, because people search for the current year. Update the post first, then change the year in the title tag, H1 and meta description. Leave it out of the URL.
  4. Leave your name off when you need the space. Google already shows it above the link.
  5. Check clicks in Search Console after 6 to 8 weeks before you change it again.
  6. Google sometimes rewrites titles. If it does, make yours shorter and closer to the H1.

95 of your 292 blog posts have titles over 60 characters, so start with the ones that get visits.

4

Write Meta Descriptions That Finish the Sale

The meta description doesn’t move your ranking directly. It helps the person decide between you and the next result.

What it isThe gray text under the blue link
Where people see itGoogle results. Not on your page.
Where you change it in HubSpotPage: Settings, then General, then Meta description
Post: Settings, then Meta description
The ruleAbout 150 characters: who it’s for, what they get, next step

5

Use the H1 to Tell Them They’re in the Right Place

Now they’ve clicked. The H1 is the first thing they read on your page, so it should match what they searched and say what makes you different.

What it isThe main heading on the page
Where people see itOn your page, at the top. Not in Google’s listing.
Where you change it in HubSpotPage editor: click the big heading and check it’s set to H1
The ruleOne per page, with the keyword in a sentence that sounds normal

6

Build the Page in the Right Order

A page ranks when it answers the search, and it converts when it deals with the owner’s problem. The H2s are the headings for each section.

What it isH2s are section headings. H3s go under them.
Where people see itOn your page
Where you change it in HubSpotPage editor: set each heading to H2 or H3
The ruleUse the keyword or a close version in 2 or 3 H2s

Your homepage design, with notes

  1. Hero. Who you help, where, and the next step
  2. Quick links. One tap to each service page
  3. Trust band. Awards and ratings in text, so AI tools can read them
  4. Pain points. The owner’s problem in their words
  5. Third option. What makes you different
  6. What you get. Each service, linked to its page
  7. First year. What changes after they sign up
  8. Industries. Links to each industry page
  9. Team. Named CPAs with credentials
  10. Reviews. Real words from clients, as text
  11. Price estimator. A smaller step for people who aren’t ready
  12. Questions. FAQs that Google and AI can quote
  13. Form. On the page, so they don’t click away
  14. Videos and articles. Your YouTube channel and best posts

Scroll inside the picture. The yellow notes say why each section is there.

H2s in this design that use the keyword

  • What Do You Get From One Team of Indianapolis CPAs?
  • Meet the Indianapolis CPAs Who’ll Know Your Business
  • What Owners Want to Know Before Calling Indianapolis CPAs

Do this

  1. Use this order for service and industry pages. Leave out what you don’t need.
  2. Read only the H2s from top to bottom. They should tell the story on their own.
  3. Write the first paragraph so someone who reads only that knows who you help and where.
7

Put the Keyword in the URL and Describe Your Images

The keyword belongs in the URL of every page except the homepage. It shows people and Google what the page is about before they click.

URLs

What it isThe page’s address
Where people see itGoogle results and the browser bar
Where you change it in HubSpotPage: Settings, then General, then Page URL
The ruleThe keyword, in lowercase with hyphens, and nothing extra
PageKeywordURL nowURL to use
Our Servicessmall business accounting indianapolis/accounting-tax-payroll/indianapolis-small-business-accounting
Monthly Accountingaccounting services indianapolisNew page/indianapolis-accounting-services
Bookkeepingbookkeeping services indianapolisNew page/indianapolis-bookkeeping-services
Payrollpayroll services indianapolis/payroll-services/indianapolis-payroll-services
Taxtax services indianapolisNew page/indianapolis-tax-services
Dentaldental cpaNew page/dental-cpa
Restaurantsrestaurant accountant/restaurant-services/restaurant-accountant
Carmelcarmel cpa/locations/carmel-indiana/carmel-cpa

The words can be in a different order from the search. Leave out small words like “in” and “the.” For a blog post, use the topic, such as /blog/indiana-sales-tax, and skip the year so you can update it. Keep the URL on older posts that already get visits.

If you change a live URL, redirect the old one the same day. In HubSpot that’s Settings, then Content, then Domains & URLs, then URL Redirects. Without it, you lose the rankings and links the old page earned.

Image alt text

What it isA short description of a photo
Where people see itHidden. Screen readers and Google read it.
Where you change it in HubSpotClick the image, then Alt text
The ruleDescribe what’s in the photo
Don’tDo
IMG_4021Dan Enge, CPA, going over a tax project calendar with a client
indianapolis cpa cpas indianapolis accountantTMA accountant meeting with a small business owner in Indianapolis

Do this

  1. Rename image files before you upload them.
  2. Add alt text to real photos. Decorative shapes can stay blank.
  3. Combine or redirect the two posts with the same title, “Federal Tax News for Individuals.”
8

Link Your Pages to Each Other

Links inside your site show Google which pages matter and help a reader get from an article to the service. This is one of the biggest fixes on your site.

What it isA link from one of your pages to another
Where people see itOn your page
Where you change it in HubSpotHighlight the words, then Insert link
The ruleLink words that say where the link goes
280
of 292 posts don’t link to a service, industry or location page in the article
166
don’t link to another post
165
have no other post linking to them

How it should work

Posts link up to the service. The service links across to its locations and industries. Related posts link to each other.

  1. Add 1 or 2 service, industry or location links to each post, high up where people will see them.
  2. Add 2 or 3 related posts to each service and industry page.

  4. Don’t use “click here,” because it tells Google nothing.
  5. Update links that go through a redirect. We found 23 addresses linked on your site that redirect, and none that were broken.

What it isLabels written in code (called JSON-LD)
Where people see itHidden in the page
Where you change it in HubSpotSettings, then Advanced, then Head HTML
The ruleOnly label what’s really on the page

Do this

  1. Fix the pricing page first. A line break inside one FAQ answer stops Google reading it.
  2. Add Service schema to every “Not yet” service page.
  3. Don’t expect FAQ drop-downs in Google. They’re mostly limited to government and health sites now, but the labels still help.
  4. Skip star ratings for your own reviews. Google doesn’t show them.
11

Make Your Pages Load Faster

A slow page loses people before they read it. When we tested the dental checklist page for your ads report, it took 8.9 seconds on a phone.

HubSpot (your site)

HubSpot already does caching and fast delivery. You need to control what gets added: big images, videos, pop-ups and tracking scripts.

WordPress

We use NitroPack, a plugin that handles caching, images and code. Use it if you ever move the site to WordPress.

What the test tells you

ScoreWhat it meansAim for
LCPHow long the main content takes to show2.5 seconds or less
INPHow quickly it reacts to a tap200 milliseconds or less
CLSHow much the page jumps while loading0.1 or less

Do this

  1. Run the homepage, checklist and playbook pages through pagespeed.web.dev and look at Mobile.
  2. Resize photos to the size they show, and keep most under 200 KB.
  3. Show a picture of the video first, and load the player when someone clicks.
  4. Remove old tags in Tag Manager and any pop-up you don’t need.
  5. Test again after each change so you know what helped.
12

Earn Better Backlinks

A backlink is a link to you from another site. Google treats a good one like a referral, so one from a trusted local site can be worth more than thousands from sites nobody visits.

Score 0 to 2 (little value)
6,055
Score 3 to 19
213
Score 20 or higher
45

The 6,313 sites that link to you, by SEMrush authority score. Your overall score is 26 and OnTarget CPA’s is 21, so you aren’t behind. The next links need to come from better sites.

Good links OnTarget has

Inc., Built In, WISH-TV, Yellow Pages and Superpages are in their strongest links, and we didn’t see them in yours.

Where to get them

TypeFor youFirst stepWho
DirectoriesYellow Pages, Superpages, chambersClaim the listingYou
PartnersRestaurant365, iSolvedAsk to be on their partner pageYou
AssociationsDental and restaurant groupsOffer a guest articleYou
Local newsWISH-TV, Indianapolis business pressSend Tyler’s take on a tax changeYou or an agency
PodcastsShows for dentists and restaurant ownersPitch one topic with a video clipYou or an agency
Useful toolsYour price estimator and scorecardAsk partners to link to themYou
Paid link buildingArticles on other sitesChoose a providerAn agency, or The HOTH

Doing it yourself or paying for it

An agency usually does this for you. You can also pay a company like The HOTH directly. Ask to approve each site first, check that it gets real visitors, and add a few links a month. Google can ignore or penalize links that look bought, so skip cheap packages with hundreds of links.

Do this

  1. Do the directories and partners first, since they’re free.
  2. Send links to your service and industry pages as well as the homepage.
  3. Let most links use your name. Use the keyword only some of the time.
  4. Keep a sheet with the site, page, date and cost.
